name: Paygent Connect

field_reviews.reason: Confirmed proprietary scheme: mutual-TLS client certificate (.pfx/.pem) plus connection ID and connection-ID password, with credentials issued through the merchant administrator site. Corroborated by the official test-environment setup manual and by independent integrator documentation (CS-Cart and ebisumart both configure マーチャントID/接続ID/接続IDパスワード plus client cert).
No OAuth, API key, or standard token scheme is documented anywhere public; everything points to the client-cert + connection ID/password scheme. 'custom' is the correct classification.

Official onboarding page (paygent.co.jp/payment_service/connect/) re-checked live: inquiry, hearing/quote from a sales rep, application via the merchant administrator site, mailed stamped application with official corporate documents, screening by each payment institution (~6 weeks guideline), then test and production environments. Unambiguously contact_sales with underwriting.

Specifications are only downloadable from the login-gated merchant administrator site after contract (official FAQ), so breadth genuinely cannot be assessed from public sources. 'unknown' is the honest value and the draft correctly treated login-gating as not proof of absence.

The integration is the PaygentB2BModule SDK (Composer package paygent/connect) wrapping a proprietary HTTPS POST 'telegram' (denshin) interface with versioned message formats — integrator docs expose a 電文バージョン (telegram version) parameter. 'sdk_only' is right; 'rest' is a loose label the draft itself flags in uncertainty_notes as meaning plain HTTPS server-to-server calls, not a RESTful API. Correct in substance, imprecise in labeling.

Value is correct but the draft provided no evidence URL for the MCP claim. My own searches for 'Paygent MCP' return only unrelated products that coincidentally share the name (FoxRick/paygentic-sdk agent-payments MCP, docs.paygent.to LLM cost-tracking SDK, paygent.net wallet assistant) — none belong to the Japanese PSP at paygent.co.jp, whose official site offers no MCP or public developer program. Composio toolkit absence re-confirmed: docs.composio.dev/toolkits/paygent returns 404.

Integration is technically possible via the contracted module/telegram interface, but only after sales contact, paper application, and per-payment-method institutional screening; nothing is buildable without a merchant contract.
The contract-plus-screening onboarding is the defining blocker, confirmed on the official onboarding page.

notes: Right-product check (the key risk): the assignment hint said 'paygent (NMI-powered)', but my independent searches confirm the draft's finding that Paygent (paygent.co.jp, Mitsubishi UFJ Nicos / DeNA joint venture) has no connection to NMI, and 'paygent/connect' is Paygent's own Composer package for its module-type integration — so the Japanese PSP researched in the draft is the correct product and the hint appears wrong. Searches for a Paygent MCP surface only unrelated same-name products (paygentic-sdk, docs.paygent.to, paygent.net), supporting none_found; that field is PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED only because the draft shipped it without an evidence URL. Also re-verified the official onboarding flow live and the contract-gated documentation FAQ.
